'''Kekistan''' is a fictional country invented on 4chan, adopted as a joke ethnicity in January 2017, and carried as a flag at American political rallies from April 2017 onward — including into the '''United States Capitol on 6 January 2021'''. It is the national-identity wing of the '''[[Cult of Kek]]''': where the cult supplies the god, Kekistan supplies the flag, the anthem and the passport.

Everything about it is documented and dated, and nothing about it is ancient. Its flag is a '''point-for-point parody of the Nazi-era German war ensign'''. Its national anthem is a '''1986 Italo-disco single'''. Its history is a self-declared fiction about conquering two invented countries named as insults. This page gives the paper trail, because the paper trail is the whole of the subject.

[[File:kekistan-flag.svg|The flag of Kekistan. Green ground in place of the Reichskriegsflagge's red, the 4chan clover in the canton in place of the Iron Cross, and a KEK device in place of the swastika disc. Vector artwork by Kevin Marks, 2017, released into the public domain.]]

== The paper trail ==

* '''December 2015''' — a flag file named '''"kekistan.jpg"''' is submitted to 4chan's '''/int/''' (International) board. This is the earliest dated artefact of the name as a flag. The name itself had been floated for imaginary places repeatedly before this.
* '''14 December 2016''' — a /pol/ thread about buying a Caribbean island; several users propose '''"Kekistan"''' as the name for it.
* '''30 January 2017''' — the YouTuber known as '''"Sargon of Akkad"''' tweets that shitposters meet the British government's criteria for an ethnicity and says he will register the group on the British census. After asking his followers for a name he settles on '''"Kekistani"''', describing the group as a "disparate and dispossessed people". ''(Know Your Meme does not use his legal name and neither does this page. The attribution and the date are Know Your Meme's and are '''not independently confirmed''' here.)''
* '''Within 48 hours''' — the "Republic of Kekistan" Twitter feed passes 5,000 followers; '''kekistan.com''' launches with a "Kek manifesto"; '''#FreeKekistan''' spreads; r/kekistan launches; and "Shadilay" is uploaded as "The National Anthem of Kekistan".
* '''1 February 2017''' — an Encyclopedia Dramatica page is created.
* '''12 September 2017''' — Bungie removes a gauntlet from ''Destiny 2'' for sharing "elements with a hate symbol"; ''Polygon'' and ''Kotaku'' describe the Kekistan flag as an alt-right or white-nationalist symbol.

'''So the coinage window is narrow and visible: a filename in December 2015, a place-name in December 2016, an ethnicity on 30 January 2017, and a national infrastructure of Twitter feed, website, subreddit, manifesto, hashtag and anthem inside two days of that.''' Four weeks from a joke to a nation.

== The fictional history ==

Kekistanis are said to have "invaded and overthrew" two invented countries, '''"Normistan"''' and '''"Cuckistan"''' — the first named for "normies", the second for a slur. They adopted the internet personality Gordon Hurd, in his "Big Man Tyrone" persona, as a jokey president. The SPLC describes Kekistan as "a satirical fictional kingdom said to have been overwhelmed by 'Normistan'" and a second, slur-derived "istan".

That is the entire national history, and it is declared as fiction by the people who wrote it. There is no claimed antiquity, no claimed territory and no claimed diaspora. '''Anyone asserting an ancient basis for Kekistan is contradicting the sources inside the movement, not only the ones outside it.'''

== The flag ==

This is the part that matters, and it is also the part on which every source agrees without hedging.

'''The source flag''' is the '''Reichskriegsflagge''' — the Nazi-era German war ensign: a '''red''' ground, an '''Iron Cross''' in the canton, an off-centre '''swastika''' disc, 3:5 proportions.

'''The Kekistan flag substitutes, element for element:'''

* '''Green''' in place of the red ground.
* The '''4chan clover''' in the canton in place of the Iron Cross.
* A '''KEK device''' — the letters arranged as a roundel — in place of the swastika disc.

The sources, in their own words:

* Wikipedia: the flag "is modeled after the '''Nazi war flag'''", with "the red becomes green, the Iron Cross becomes the 4chan logo, and '''the swastika replaced by a rubric for KEK'''".
* SPLC, cataloguing the symbols carried at Charlottesville: the flag "mimics a German Nazi war flag, with the Kek logo replacing the swastika and the green replacing the infamous German red", with a 4chan logo in the canton — and "'''Alt-righters are particularly fond of the way the banner trolls liberals who recognize its origins.'''"

That last clause is the design's stated function in the words of its sympathisers' own cataloguers: '''the resemblance is not an accident and it is not deniable, because the recognition is the point.''' A parody flag works only if the original is recognised. This page reproduces the flag because explaining the subject requires showing it, and captions it as what it is.

== The anthem ==

'''"Shadilay"''' is a real record: a 1986 Italo-disco single by the Italian band '''P.E.P.E.''', released on the '''Magic Sound''' label, whose sleeve shows '''a green frog holding a magic wand'''.

* '''17 November 2009''' — first YouTube upload.
* '''September 2016''' — /pol/ finds it. A "/pol/ exclusive" repost on '''13 September 2016''' is followed by remixes on the 14th, 15th and 16th. On '''15 September 2016''' the insider blog ''The Truth About Pepe the Frog and the Cult of Kek'' calls it "Kek/Pepe's musical anthem".
* '''19 October 2016''' — an Urban Dictionary entry.
* '''9 November 2016''' — the day after the election, a user posts the lyrics to /pol/.
* '''Late January 2017''' — re-uploaded as "The National Anthem of Kekistan".

'''The coincidence is genuine.''' A band called P.E.P.E., in 1986, on a label called Magic Sound, with a wand-wielding green frog on the sleeve, is a real object and nobody made it up. Adherents cite it as evidence of '''memetic synchronicity''', and it is the single strongest-feeling item in the whole corpus.

It is also exactly the kind of coincidence that becomes available when a very large number of people search very hard for one. Both of those statements are true, and a page that gives only one of them is not being straight with the reader. The record exists; what it demonstrates is a separate question from whether it exists.

== Where the flag has been carried ==

* '''April 2017''' — the Berkeley protests. Kekistan flags are documented at the 15 April 2017 rally; the people carrying them are in ordinary clothes.
* '''1 May 2017''' — the May Day demonstrations at Foley Square, New York.
* '''4 June 2017''' — the Portland Free Speech Rally.
* '''12 August 2017''' — the "Unite the Right" rally in Charlottesville, where "Kekistani" appears as a listed group on the rally's "Join, or Die" poster.
* '''16 September 2017''' — the "Mother of All Rallies" on the National Mall in Washington DC, where a '''man in a green robe''' was filmed discussing the flag. The journalist Baynard Woods, who was there, wrote that he "talked to one guy who carries a flag and wears a green robe, but he had nothing much to say before scampering off", and describes a second man whose T-shirt showed "a green fist rising up above the word 'Kekistan'".
* '''18 November 2017''' — an anti-fascist rally on Boston Common, where the flag was '''worn as a cape''' by a counter-demonstration's subject, and where hand-lettered placards read "NO KEK NO KKK".
* '''4 August 2018''' — a Patriot Prayer rally in Portland, Oregon, where police confiscated sticks, shields, pepper spray, fireworks and '''a baseball bat wrapped in a Kekistan flag'''.
* '''6 January 2021''' — the '''attack on the United States Capitol'''. A photograph of the Kek flag inside the building opens Matt Sheedy's essay for the Smithsonian-partnered ''Uncivil Religion'' project.

[[File:kekistan-flag-cape-boston-2017.jpg|The Kekistan flag worn as a cape, Boston Common, 18 November 2017 — the KEK roundel, which stands in the position of the swastika disc on the flag it parodies. Photo: Marc Nozell, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.]]

=== The Green Kek Warrior ===

The best-known photograph of a person in Kekistani costume was taken at the '''Portland rally of 4 August 2018'''. The man wore a bright-green bandana tied across the eyes, over the bridge of the nose; a long green gauntlet and green gloves; dark teal trousers with a loose green overskirt; a black mesh athletic vest; and carried, low at his side, a '''round green shield painted with the KEK logo'''. The internet named him the "Green Kek Warrior". The photographs circulated as mockery rather than as coverage, and one of the most-shared edits put him beside a cartoon character in a similar green mask under the caption "Worst. White supremacist rally. Ever."

Three points of accuracy, each of which is usually got wrong:

* '''It is one man, not a group.''' The images that appear to show several people in green are different crops and different dunk-edits of the same two or three frames of the same individual. No photographed group of green Kek costumes exists in the record, and this library looked for one.
* '''He has never been publicly identified.''' No reporting names him. Nothing is asserted here beyond the bare fact that he was photographed in costume at that rally.
* '''The photographs cannot be reproduced.''' Every one is an uncredited phone photograph circulated on Twitter and mirrored by a meme database; there is no licence and no identifiable rights-holder, and no openly-licensed equivalent exists anywhere — there is no file of him on Wikimedia Commons. So this page describes the costume in prose and links to the archive.

Searches for the other things people remember — green morphsuits, full-body frog costumes, green-costumed groups at the 2016–17 rallies — turned up '''no evidence''' of any of them. Pepe '''masks''' are documented, but at the 2019 Hong Kong pro-democracy protests, a completely different political context. See [[Pepe the Frog]].

== One item in the archive that establishes nothing ==

On '''16 November 2018''' the ''Daytona Beach News-Journal'' reported that a 15-year-old had been charged with the first-degree premeditated murder of his mother, and a BuzzFeed News reporter posted a screenshot showing a Kekistani flag as the cover image of the accused's Facebook page. It is recorded here because it is in the archive and because leaving it out would be a selective reading. '''It establishes nothing causal and should not be used as though it did.'''

== What is not established ==

* '''"Sargon of Akkad"''' as the coiner of "Kekistani" — dated to 30 January 2017 by Know Your Meme, not independently confirmed here.
* An '''ADL designation''' of Kekistan or of the Kekistan flag. This library searched adl.org and found none. The ADL's designation is of '''Pepe''', with caveats — see [[Cult of Kek]] §10. The SPLC is the organisation that treated Kekistan directly.
* A '''white-supremacist backronym''' for "Kekistan", reported in a 2017 Al Jazeera far-right glossary. Sourced only to advocacy and press, and not verified here.
* The '''Flags of the World''' entry on the Kekistan flag, which this library saw only in search-result snippets and treats as corroborative at best.

== Coverage ==
The dated paper trail from the December 2015 "kekistan.jpg" file on /int/, through the 14 December 2016 /pol/ island thread, the 30 January 2017 "Kekistani" coinage and the 48-hour build-out of Twitter feed, website, manifesto, subreddit, hashtag and anthem, to the February 2017 Encyclopedia Dramatica page and the September 2017 ''Destiny 2'' removal. The self-declared fictional history of "Normistan" and "Cuckistan" and the jokey presidency. The flag as a point-for-point parody of the Nazi-era ''Reichskriegsflagge'' — green for red, the 4chan clover for the Iron Cross, the KEK device for the swastika disc — quoted from Wikipedia and the SPLC, including the SPLC's note that the recognisability is the design's appeal, with the flag reproduced from a public-domain vector and captioned as what it is. The anthem's real origin as a 1986 Italo-disco single by P.E.P.E. on Magic Sound with a frog-and-wand sleeve, its dated September 2016 discovery, and both halves of the honest reading of the coincidence. Where the flag has been carried, from Berkeley in April 2017 to the United States Capitol on 6 January 2021. The Green Kek Warrior described in prose with the three usual errors corrected — one man not a group, never publicly identified, photographs unlicensed and therefore not reproduced — and the negative findings on morphsuits and costumed groups. One criminal item recorded as establishing nothing. A closing list of what is not established, including that there is no ADL designation of Kekistan.
